subject: Clarify billing for microburst short-chat interactions
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medix.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing for microburst interactions (short chats)

Hi Hannah,

Quick question from procurement as we scope the pilot: our Cortex agents generate a lot of micro-interactions — many requests are ~20-60 tokens (single-turn question -> short answer). Can you confirm how Redwood will bill those? Specifically:

- Do you round up to a minimum token quantum per request? If so, what is the quantum?
- If multiple short requests happen within a short window (e.g., 10 requests in 5 minutes), do you aggregate or do we get charged per call?
- Any packaging/discounts that apply to heavy microburst traffic vs. long-context sessions?

We're trying to model expected monthly spend and want to make sure we don't get surprised by rounding at scale. If you have a short example calculation that would be great.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Lee
Director, Procurement
Medix Solutions

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medix.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 10:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing for microburst interactions (short chats)

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers first, then a couple of worked examples. Happy to hop on a quick screen-share if you'd like to walk numbers together.

Summary:
- Minimum quantum: billing is evaluated in 100-token quanta for "per-request" metering. We bill in 100-token increments for requests that are not eligible for prefix/KV reuse.
- Aggregation: requests from the same session (same session id) within a 30-minute window are eligible for context reuse. That means the input prompt context (prefix tokens) can be deduplicated for billing and the KV-cache reuse reduces billed tokens for subsequent calls.
- Discounts/packaging: committed-volume packages reduce the per-100-token price and we offer a microburst pilot credit (one-time) and smoothing for the first 2 billing cycles on new commitments.

Worked examples (simplified):
1) Single-turn micro request (no reuse)
- Actual tokens: prompt 18 + completion 32 = 50 tokens
- Billed: rounds up to 100-token quantum => billed tokens = 100

2) Series of 10 micro requests within 10 minutes from same session id (prefix reuse applies)
- First call: prompt 18 + completion 32 = 50 => billed as 100 (includes context setup)
- Subsequent 9 calls: prompt 18 (same prefix cached) + completion 30 = 48 tokens each. With KV reuse, we bill for completion tokens only (we charge for output tokens + a small metadata delta, effectively ~50% savings depending on model). Conservatively assume billed per subsequent call = 50 tokens => rounds up to 100 quantum? In practice, we apply aggregation rules: after prefix reuse recognized, small outputs are aggregated into minute-level batches and charged pro-rata; for these examples you will typically see billed ~50 tokens per subsequent call, which the billing UI will present as 9 * 50 = 450 => combined billed tokens ~550 (vs. 10*100=1000 if no reuse).

3) Impact of committed package
- If you commit to a 200k-token/month package we drop the per-100-token rate by 18% and provide a one-time pilot microburst credit of 50k tokens for the first month.

Notes & next steps:
- For clients instrumenting sessions, we recommend attaching a session_id to calls so you get full benefit of prefix/KV reuse.
- If you cannot attach session ids, we treat calls independently for metering.
- I'll attach a spreadsheet with scenario modeling (attached).

Attaching: redwood-billing-examples.xlsx (worked examples + spreadsheet you can tweak).

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Billing for microburst interactions (Medix) — recommended concession

Vanessa / Ben — forwarding Medix's ask. Key points: they expect many short calls and are sensitive to rounding. My recommendation for a pilot-friendly concession (to close the PoC):

- Offer: 20% off list per-100-token rate on a 3-month pilot if they sign a 3-month minimum commitment of 200k tokens/month (MDX-2025-87).
- Promotional credit: one-time 50k microburst credit (applied first invoice) to offset rounding for the first month.
- Implementation: require session_id instrumentation to enable KV/prefix reuse; if they can't, we'll reduce the discount to 10% (higher risk).
- Legal/Finance ask: waive minimum for months 2 and 3 if product fails to meet defined availability SLA (we'll draft a short clause).

Rationale: preserves unit economics while addressing their rounding concerns. If you're good with the credit + 20% per-100-token discount, I'll send a short amendment and the example table.

Attaching draft terms for internal review: MDX-pilot-terms-draft.pdf

Hannah

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing for microburst interactions (short chats) — pilot proposal

Jordan — thanks for the prompt. Per internal review, here's a concrete pilot offer that addresses the microburst rounding concern.

Offer summary:
- Commitment: 3-month pilot commitment at 200k tokens/month (MDX-2025-87).
- Unit pricing: billed in 100-token quanta as outlined (same metering rules). Committed price = list-price * 0.80 (20% discount).
- Pilot credit: one-time 50k-token microburst credit applied to month 1 invoice to offset rounding headroom.
- Session instrumentation: to get aggregation benefits, integrate session_id in calls (we'll share a small SDK snippet). If session_id is not available, we reserve the right to apply standard per-call rounding with a reduced discount (10%).
- SLA carve: we will draft a short SLA addendum — if availability drops below 99.5% for the pilot, we'll waive month 2 minimum.

Illustrative math (month 1, conservative):
- Expected actual tokens processed: 300k (many microbursts).
- Without reuse and without discounts: rounding could inflate billed tokens to ~400k (worst case).
- With session prefix reuse + our pilot credit and 20% discount: estimated billed tokens after aggregation = ~350k; applied credit (50k) -> invoiceable = 300k * discounted rate.

Next steps:
1) If you confirm, we'll issue a 1-page pilot amendment (DocuSign) and share the integration snippet.
2) We'll provision a pilot project in our sandbox region and enable detailed token-level reporting for the pilot.

Would you like me to send the DocuSign now or do you prefer to sync for 20 minutes to walk the spreadsheet?

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
